findings: All 65 selected exit replies reviewed in context. No questions survive the filters; semantic failures remain in role tracking and context-specific send-offs. Short two-sentence closings are accepted unless they add a material defect.

Reviewed all 62 selected stop replies. Seven criticals survive regex: physical-presence claims, forbidden-topic continuation, denial of a visible spoiler, and continued advice/content after stop requests. Three-sentence repetitive acknowledgments excluded as unsuitable training targets.

All 64 selected quiet_support replies reviewed in context. No questions or advice survive the filters and no robot-context presence claims appear; failures are garbled or meaning-inverting metaphors, misstated facts (scrape as loss, sprain as cannot walk, home as prison), invented details and stock you're-not-alone reassurance. The teacher leans on quiet as a tic across many replies; acceptable singly but worth a cap in the merged corpus.

All 74 selected low_energy replies reviewed in context. This is the cleanest v3 family: replies are short, question-free and drop the earlier topic as asked, and no robot-context replies claim physical actions. Failures are invented or inaccurate facts, requested jokes that are not jokes, and over-long answers. Sample pairs are often near-duplicates (beans on toast twice for two prompts, identical goodnights), so the merged corpus should dedupe near-identical replies.

All 73 selected practical_help replies reviewed in context: 53 rejected, 2 critical, 20 kept of which 16 are mixed. The 4B teacher lacks the household and first-aid competence this family needs: it misreads the problem (lost versus swapped bag, chirp versus alarm), gives wrong or impossible steps (unplugged machines draining, sending a misdirected transfer back, wrong nosebleed pinch spot), ignores the stated constraint (charger at the office, child needing care) and still opens with questions. Even the kept replies are mediocre. Recommend excluding practical_help from admission or replacing it with human-authored replies built from the prompt expectations, rather than training on this output.

All 64 selected style_control replies reviewed in context. Single-word, single-name and plain-answer requests are handled well. Failures are exact-length misses (five, three or two word requests off by one or more), question-and-answer jokes where one sentence was asked, questions back despite instructions, wrong facts (strawberry, octopus hearts) and an invented evening for the assistant. Word-count, sentence-count and trailing-question constraints are mechanically checkable and should become automatic filters before the next teacher run.
practical_help excluded as a family by reese: all 73 selected replies rejected (53 on review, 20 by exclusion).
